object_description: modular stepped volumes forming a terraced campus framework
design_condition: Two modular volumes occupy the plots and are eroded toward the campus square, with stepped forms adapting to the slope and shaping varied outdoor spaces, but the single central entrance weakens the viaduct-side arrival.

positive.statement: The project consistently interweaves buildings and outdoor space to create an attractive and diverse campus world.

position.rationale: Distributed building edges and open areas in the top view support an outdoor-space campus anchor.

positive.statement: Staggering the volumes ensures good sunlight in the central outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: Staggered perimeter masses visibly frame central open space; sunlight performance is inferred from massing.

positive.statement: The central campus square is the heart of the complex and receives all paths.

position.rationale: A central void is clearly identifiable in plan and sits at ground level between the sampled volumes.

positive.statement: The topography is made a theme through ramps, seating steps, and stairs.

position.rationale: Stepped and irregular ground-level edges in the plan provide a plausible topographic-landscape anchor.

positive.statement: The weather-insensitive facade construction enables a long service life and reduces life-cycle costs.

position.rationale: An exposed outer building edge provides the closest sampled location for facade construction.

positive.statement: The materials are compatible with the specified ecological requirements.

position.rationale: Material compatibility is unobservable; the marker estimates a visible outer facade region.

negative.statement: The restriction to one main entrance creates an unfavorable reception situation and long distances.

position.rationale: The statement identifies a central entrance, but the sampled point cloud does not distinguish an entrance element.

negative.statement: Important district connections are missing or require large detours, and the viaduct area is unattractive as an open space.

position.rationale: The viaduct-side edge is not explicitly identifiable, so the east-side perimeter estimates the affected site area.

negative.statement: The internal circulation creates long paths, dead ends, and labyrinthine spaces.

position.rationale: Interior paths are absent from the exterior sample; this point estimates the denser left building mass.

negative.statement: The basic spatial-typological rules are unclear and the deviations are not comprehensible.

position.rationale: The irregular stepped footprint provides a broad anchor for the criticized spatial organization.

negative.statement: The huge basement has practically no daylight and many large ground-floor rooms are trapped inside the plan.

position.rationale: Basement interiors are not sampled; the marker estimates the lower central portion of the left volume.

negative.statement: Internal access is confusing and inflexible, and the lounge proportions are not optimal.

position.rationale: Interior access and lounge geometry are unseen; this estimates a plausible central-right plan zone.

negative.statement: The complicated volumetrics and extensive facade, terrace, and roof development are complex and expensive to construct and maintain.

position.target: volumetrics, facade, terrace, and roof development
position.rationale: The distinct upper-right stepped volume and roof footprint visibly support a broad complexity anchor.

negative.statement: The above-average glazing creates a relatively high overheating risk and requires substantial technical effort.

position.rationale: Glazing is not distinguishable in the point cloud; the marker estimates an exposed east-side facade.

negative.statement: The large supports in the partition walls are inconvenient and the rise zones are limited.

position.rationale: Interior supports and vertical circulation are absent; the point estimates a plausible left-volume interior zone.
